summary: A polished Old City Thai restaurant rooted in the family’s Lamphun recipes, with northern dishes alongside broader Thai cooking. Its 2026 menu is designed for sharing, and the listed prices put it above casual market meals but within a moderate restaurant spend.
whyGo: Try northern-rooted home-style recipes in an attentive, more composed setting than a street stall.
The current menu offers recognizable regional dishes such as beef cheek hang lay curry, fermented fish with egg and Chiang Mai khao soi, as well as seafood and vegetarian choices.
Share several plates family-style; the restaurant says dishes arrive as they are prepared.
bestFor: A relaxed lunch or dinner in the Old City, including groups who want to sample several dishes.
Vegetarians, with advance menu review; the restaurant lists a dedicated vegetarian menu.
skipIf: You want a very low-cost meal or a quick, single-dish stop.
You need a guaranteed gluten-free or allergy-safe kitchen without confirming details directly first.
You are planning to visit on Monday, when the Old Town branch is listed as closed.
duration: Allow about 1–1.5 hours for a shared meal (planning estimate; not a venue-published duration).
cost: The current Old Town menu lists many starters and noodles around ฿159–฿299, signature dishes from about ฿209, and premium crab or beef dishes up to ฿899. A shared meal with drinks can vary substantially; check the linked 2026 menu before setting a per-person budget. Prices may change before December.
hours: Old Town branch: Tuesday–Sunday, 11:00–16:00 (last order 14:30) and 17:00–22:00 (last order 20:30); closed Monday. The menu PDF gives slightly later kitchen cutoffs (14:40 and 20:40), so arrive earlier and confirm around your visit.
bestTime: Book a dinner or lunch table in advance, especially for weekends and holiday dates. For a less rushed meal, arrive well before the last-order cutoff.
gettingThere: At 252/13–14 Prapokklao Road in Si Phum, Chiang Mai Old City. Walk from nearby Old City accommodation, or use Grab or a red songthaew (shared taxi). The restaurant lists complimentary guest parking at Vista Hotel Chiang Mai, about a two-minute walk away; show the parking ticket to staff.
booking: The restaurant recommends booking ahead because tables are limited and says peak dates can fill. Contact the Old Town branch directly via Facebook Messenger, LINE (@baanlandai), email ([email protected]) or phone (+66 65 848 4464). Its site says it does not accept third-party online reservations; email replies usually take 1–2 business days.
accessibility: Step-free entry, accessible toilet, and seating clearances are not documented in the reviewed sources. Contact the restaurant before booking if mobility access is important. Families are welcome. Outdoor tables are not fully roofed and mosquitoes may be present in the evening.
practicalTips: Review the official Old Town menu: prices and menu effective date (1 February 2026) are shown in its PDF; ask about seasonal availability closer to travel.
The restaurant identifies plant-based/vegetarian dishes and can adjust spice for most orders. Confirm that a dish is fully vegetarian when ordering.
For gluten-free needs or nut allergies, the restaurant asks guests to contact it before reserving and may decline severe-allergy bookings.
Visa and Mastercard are accepted; American Express is not, according to the restaurant FAQ.
decemberNotes: December is a popular Chiang Mai travel period; the restaurant specifically warns that weekends and holidays can book out, so reserve directly once your date is settled. No December 2026 special hours or holiday closures were confirmed. Check the restaurant’s current hours and menu shortly before travel.
uncertainties: December 2026 operating hours, prices, menu availability and holiday closures can change; the sources reflect information available on 17 October 2026.
Official pages disagree by ten minutes on last kitchen order; this brief uses the earlier FAQ/reservation cutoff.
The sources reviewed do not establish step-free access or accessible facilities.
